E7 [Hearing -LRB-person-RRB-] From this point of view , someone who is not fully hearing has a hearing loss or is said to be hard of hearing or deaf .
E8 [Hearing -LRB-person-RRB-] The continuum of hearing ability tends to be broken down into fine gradations .
E9 [Hearing -LRB-person-RRB-] Moving down the scale and further away from the medical norm , people are classed as hearing , then slightly hard of hearing , moderately hard of hearing , severely hard of hearing , and finally deaf ( severely deaf or profoundly deaf for those furthest from the norm ) .

E1 [Block -LRB-chess-RRB-] A block is a defensive tactic in chess in response to an attack , consisting of interposing a piece between the opponent 's attacking piece and the piece being attacked .

E3 [Block -LRB-chess-RRB-] Blocking is not an option when the attacking piece is directly adjacent to the piece it is attacking , or when the attacking piece is a knight ( because knights `` jump over other pieces '' and can not be blocked ) .
E4 [Block -LRB-chess-RRB-] When an opponent 's attack on a piece is blocked , the blocking piece is to some extent pinned , either relatively or absolutely , until a future move by either side allows it to be unpinned .
E5 [Block -LRB-chess-RRB-] A check on a king by an opponent 's queen , rook , or bishop can sometimes be blocked by moving a piece to a square in line in between the opponent 's checking piece and the checked king .
E6 [Block -LRB-chess-RRB-] The blocking piece is then absolutely pinned to the king by the attacking piece .
E7 [Block -LRB-chess-RRB-] Another type of interposing in chess can involve placing a piece between two opponent 's pieces where one of those pieces is protecting the other , or they are both protecting each other .

E13 [Block book] Single-leaf woodcuts from the preceding decades often included passages of text with prayers , indulgences and other material ; the block book was an extension of this form .
